digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### The AV2 Video Standard Has Released (Final v1.0 Specification)
URL: https://av2.aomedia.org
Next-generation royalty-free video codec reaches production milestone
AV2 promises 30-50% efficiency gains over AV1, which itself beat H.265/HEVC. The Alliance for Open Media consortium (Google, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, Netflix) coordinating this spec means rapid browser and hardware decoder adoption is likely within 18-24 months. Watch for encoding infrastructure buildout as a follow-on investment theme.

### Zig ELF Linker Improvements Devlog
URL: https://ziglang.org/devlog/2026/#2026-05-30
Zig's self-hosted toolchain matures toward production readiness
The Zig team continues grinding on their custom linker, critical infrastructure for their "C without the footguns" pitch to systems programmers. Compiler toolchain improvements here matter because Zig is gaining traction in embedded, game dev, and as a C/C++ build system replacement. Bun's success (built on Zig) validates the thesis.

### Claw Patrol: an open-source security firewall for agents
URL: https://deno.com/blog/clawpatrol
Deno ships first serious attempt at runtime security for autonomous AI agents
As agents proliferate, the attack surface compounds—Deno is positioning early for the "how do we let AI act without letting it run wild" problem. This is infrastructure that didn't exist 18 months ago because the use case didn't exist. Smart platform play from the Deno team.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### OpenRouter raises $113M Series B
URL: https://openrouter.ai/announcements/series-b
API aggregation layer for LLMs hits significant funding milestone
OpenRouter sits between developers and model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source), abstracting away the complexity of multi-model orchestration. $113M for what's essentially middleware tells you VCs believe model commoditization is real and the value accrues to routing/orchestration layers. Direct read-through to model provider margin compression.

### Accenture to acquire Ookla
URL: https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2026/accenture-to-acquire-ookla-to-strengthen-network-intelligence-and-experience-with-data-and-ai-for-enterprises
Consulting giant buys Speedtest parent for network intelligence play
Ookla's dataset—billions of speed tests across every ISP and geography—is genuinely irreplaceable. Accenture gets proprietary network performance data to sell to telcos, enterprises doing hybrid work planning, and anyone betting on 5G/edge deployment. Strategic asset acquisition disguised as a consulting bolt-on.

### SoftBank says it will invest up to €75 billion to build French data centers
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/30/softbank-says-it-will-invest-up-to-e75-billion-to-build-french-data-centers/
Masayoshi Son commits to 5GW of European AI compute capacity
The number is staggering—5GW is roughly 1% of France's total electrical generation capacity. This is SoftBank's bet that AI compute demand will outstrip supply for the decade, and that European data sovereignty concerns create pricing power. Power procurement and grid access become the binding constraint, not capital.

### 'What a joke': Github Copilot's new token-based billing spurs consternation among devs
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/30/what-a-joke-github-copilots-new-token-based-billing-spurs-consternation-among-devs/
Microsoft moves Copilot from flat-rate to consumption pricing
The shift from $19/month unlimited to token-based billing is Microsoft testing how much developer productivity gains are actually worth. Heavy users subsidized light users under the old model. This repricing will accelerate exploration of open-source alternatives (Continue, Cody, Cursor) and validates that inference costs remain material.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Domain expertise has always been the real moat
URL: https://www.brethorsting.com/blog/2026/05/domain-expertise-has-always-been-the-real-moat/
Counterpoint to the "AI replaces expertise" narrative
As AI tools commoditize technical execution, the scarce resource becomes knowing what to build and why—the judgment layer. Relevant for evaluating AI startups: pure wrapper plays are vulnerable; domain-specific vertical integrations are defensible. The best AI companies will look like unusually efficient versions of domain leaders, not general-purpose platforms.

### Parallel Reconstruction of Lawful TLS Wiretapping
URL: https://remyhax.xyz/posts/reproducing-lawful-tls-wiretapping/
Security researcher reproduces state-level TLS interception techniques
Deep technical analysis of how lawful intercept actually works at the protocol level—relevant for any company with exposure to encrypted communications (messaging, enterprise security, privacy tech). The reconstruction demonstrates these capabilities are within reach of sophisticated adversaries, not just nation-states. Enterprise security posture implications are real.

### Microcode inside the Intel 8087 floating-point chip: register exchange
URL://www.righto.com/2026/05/microcode-inside-intel-8087-floating.html
Ken Shirriff continues his chip archaeology on foundational Intel hardware
Detailed reverse engineering of how Intel implemented floating-point operations in 1980. Beyond the historical interest, this series illuminates the microcode abstraction layer that modern chip vulnerabilities (Spectre-class) exploit. Understanding how we got here helps understand where the attack surface lives.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The week's signal is clear: infrastructure is repricing. SoftBank betting €75B on French power capacity, OpenRouter raising $113M to sit between models, Accenture buying Ookla for proprietary network data—the pattern is capital flowing to bottlenecks and coordination layers rather than applications. Meanwhile, GitHub's Copilot repricing and the AV2 release both point toward commoditization at the model/codec level with value capture moving to orchestration and distribution. The meta-trend is that as AI capabilities become table stakes, the moats shift to data, power, and domain expertise—exactly the boring stuff that scales poorly but compounds well.
